newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - T-bonds' defiance seen sign of strength.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bonds' defiance seen sign of strength.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures' defiance in recent sessions of expectations for a technical pullback may be underscoring the strength of the market's uptrend, technical analysts said.
Jim Grauer, president of Omnitrage, noted that the daily stochastic continued to "bounce along the ceiling", even though it was extended well beyond its typical 20-day cycle.
"The longer it goes here with these little bounces and failure to cross, the more benign the down-cycle -- maybe a shortened daily cycle which would not impede or threaten the weekly cycle," he said.
Grauer added that the weekly stochastic, which had upcrossed at deeply oversold levels a few weeks ago, was now firmly rising with the percent-K and D values widening positively.

The weekly sometimes vacillates near a K/D cross, but the behavior in the past two weeks has been very strong and boded well for a long-awaited upcross in the monthly stochastic, probably by the end of the month, he said.
In the very near term, the 60-minute and 100-minute stochastics were inching higher, and it might take another day or two before a correction began, Grauer said.
He said the 107-109 area was becoming a strong support for June T-bond futures.

The June contract was up slightly on the day, hovering just below Friday's 110-14/32 high in late morning trade. Analysts said the market was shrugging off a sharp drop in the dollar since late last week.

John Gambino, of JBG Technical Analysis, said the contract could probe the 111-1/2 to 112 area before seeing a correction. That target was his projection for the fifth wave of the market's five-wave sequence that started from the April 11 low of 106-12/32.
Gambino added that the big down move from early December highs had been an A-B-C correction and that he expected the market to rally again after a brief pullback.
In Elliott Wave theory, five-wave moves generally occur in the direction of the underlying trend, while three-wave moves tend to be corrective.

Despite the perceived softness in Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's recent remarks, many in the market still believe the Fed will tighten credit at its May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting. But even with a rate hike, the long end of the curve could react positively, Grauer said.
